Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t & =-{\int }_{3}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-⟨5,\,-1,\,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying the vector addition rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)+⟨-1,\,1,\,-1⟩\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{3}⟨-1,\,1,\,-1⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨-5,\,1,\,2⟩+{⟨-t,\,t,\,-t⟩|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =⟨-5,\,1,\,2⟩+⟨-3,\,3,\,-3⟩\text{ } \\  & =⟨-8,\,4,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
